theDifferenceThatWasFoundAndWhyThePredic.measuredShape: Every one of the 21,437 is on maxFootprintSqFt, and every one is exactly +/-0.01 sq ft (histograms: 48055 245 x +0.01 / 145 x -0.01; 48209 462 / 149; 48453 7721 / 7526; 48491 3141 / 2048 -- nothing else). 48021 and 48309 have no footprint cells at all and 0 changes.
theDifferenceThatWasFoundAndWhyThePredic.rootCause: A footprint cell has no independent source: it is area x coverage. The ORIGINAL write computed the value from the raw geometry and stored inputs.parcelAreaSqFt already rounded to 2 dp. Re-deriving from the recorded 2-dp area therefore differs from the stored value by up to 0.005 sqft rounding, which the writer's own rounding turns into exactly +/-0.01. The pin moved NO coverage value (measured: 0 of the 509,152 height+coverage cells move), so the 0.01 is the RECORD's precision, not the corpus's law.
theDifferenceThatWasFoundAndWhyThePredic.decision: A footprint whose recorded coverage input still equals the pinned coverage CARRIES its stored value (citation and dates move, the number does not) -- which is what 'the pinned row gives the same numbers' means, and what the dispatch's own prediction assumes. When the recorded coverage input HAS moved, the footprint is re-derived from the recorded area and that move is reported as a value change like any other. Implemented as releasedFootprintTarget; pinned by falsifier 6 with a paired control.
theDifferenceThatWasFoundAndWhyThePredic.soTheSecondPrediction: 709,945 re-stamps / 0 value changes, which is the dispatch's prediction. Recorded here so that a reader sees the 21,437 rather than only its resolution: a plain re-derivation would have shipped 21,437 customer-visible +/-0.01 sq ft moves with no law behind them, and the dry run would have disagreed with the dispatch without this note.

adversarialNotesOnThisDesign: The release leans entirely on the source prefix, which is why the identity claim is asserted against the tree rather than commented: if a future writer composes a corpus source on an envelope rail, the release would start moving its cells, and the identity suite is what makes that visible.

The release is per RAIL, unlike P-363's per parcel. That is forced, not preferred: this job gates its three corpus rails independently per field and a parcel routinely carries a value beside an absence (measured: 4,961 Lockhart parcels). What is kept from P-363 is the property that matters -- no rail is ever HALF-moved: a rail moves only when its OWN recorded inputs are readable, and a rail that is not movable is named (`blocked`) and left exactly as it stands.

The footprint carry is a deliberate exception to re-derivation, and it is the one place a reader should be suspicious. It is bounded by two conditions (the target must be a value, and the recorded coverage input must equal the pinned coverage), and falsifier 6's paired control proves the release still re-derives when the input moves. If the pinned coverage ever changes, the carry stops applying for that cell.

A re-stamp moves `updated_at` (the UPDATE's SET clause). Intended -- the citation really did change -- but the seat's blast-radius expectations should say that up to 709,945 rows' timestamps move on the apply.

The re-resolution uses the cell's own recorded (jurisdictionKey, districtCode), never the live zoningDistrict cell: a parcel whose zoning changed since its envelope cells were written keeps the old code until the zoning rail's own change lands. Deliberate, and named in the job header's bypass list.

The new-refusal branch is the one that could interact with OPS-24 Law 7 (an `unaccounted` cell on a slated rail flips the county's ledger values back to the bake). It writes the writer's existing disposition for that rail and never `unaccounted`; the dry run reports newRefusal per county so the seat can see the number before applying.
